newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeder cattle steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeder cattle steady.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from up 0.100 cent per lb to off 0.100 while feeder cattle were expected to open steady, analysts said.

Some carryover support in nearby months is expected following wintry weather in some parts of the country. Cold weather has moved down into the southern and central Plains which could limit weight gains, analysts said.

However, a continued weak tone to choice beef prices may again weigh on sentiment. Beef sales were active last week, particularly Friday, when the lightweight choice price dipped to its lowest level since September 5, sources noted.
USDA reported sales on 392 loads of fabricated cuts Friday. Also, choice, yield-grade 3 carcasses weighing 550 to 700 lbs were quoted $0.78 per cwt lower at $104.30.

Trading may become lighter as the week progresses and Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report draws closer. Early expectations on the report indicate continued large placements into feedlots during November and feedlot supplies now above year-ago levels.
Feeder cattle futures will likely continue to follow live cattle, especially since some feeder auction markets close for the holiday period, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.15 at $65.02 per cwt.
